thread_analysis.thread_summary: This thread (July 2022 - February 2025) traces the entire Bluetooth certification journey of a 'Holfee' product family (gateway + multiple sensors) by Nippon Seiki ([COMPANY]), from initial inquiry through repeated derivative model additions over multiple years. It begins with an initial quote inquiry comparing SoC-direct-mounting vs. pre-certified module paths (July 2022), then proceeds to certification of an initial sensor model (initial RF PHY test, design registration, Product List addition, Compliance Folder), and then covers a series of derivative model scenarios: LC matching circuit changes (requiring 2-item RF PHY test for derivative), board size/component addition changes with unchanged BLE FW and antenna path (free derivative, no test), enclosure size changes (free Bluetooth derivative but separate Japanese Radio Act re-application required), design changes with unchanged Model Numbers (no registration action if Model Number is already in Product List and is findable in SIG's database), and artwork-only changes (buzzer circuit, programming connector, free derivative). In February 2025, the customer returned when the Bluetooth SIG replaced Launch Studio with Qualification Workspace, rendering prior procedure documents obsolete - the consultant provided updated procedure documents and navigation guidance for the new portal.
all_questions_found: Does directly mounting a BLE SoC (IC chip) on the PCB instead of a pre-certified module require RF PHY testing and design registration, and what does it cost?
If the LC matching (antenna matching) circuit is changed but nothing else in the BLE path is modified, does the new variant still qualify as a derivative, and what test is needed?

If our board size, casing size, non-BLE components, and/or PCB artwork change but the BLE FW and BLE-to-antenna path are unchanged, can we add the variant to the Product List for free as a derivative with no additional test?
A design-changed variant has the same Model Number as the base - can't be added as a duplicate to the Product List. Does this mean there is a compliance issue?
The board/enclosure size change qualifies as a free Bluetooth derivative - but does Japan's Radio Act (工事設計認証) require re-application?
The SIG website UI changed and we can no longer follow the derivative addition procedure we received. Where can we find our existing registrations, and is there an updated procedure document?

The SIG registration name and product model name must completely match - does this mean the Model Number we publish must match the nameplate/label/manual model number on the actual shipped product, and do we need a separate Product List entry per color code?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread introduces the SoC vs. module distinction for certification paths: SoC-direct-mount requires product-level RF PHY test (27 items for required+2M+Coded) + design registration; module use allows referencing the module's Component QDID, skipping product-level RF PHY. For derivative model eligibility, the key rule applied consistently: 'same FW on MCU and BLE chip AND unchanged BLE-antenna path components/routing = free derivative with no test'; 'LC matching change only = derivative but requires 2-item RF PHY test (¥180,000)'. Japan's Radio Act 工事設計認証 is a completely separate requirement that requires re-application per model name if board shape or external appearance changes - proactively flagged alongside Bluetooth qualification. SIG compliance enforcement works via database search by Model Number: if the label's model number is in the Product List, the product is compliant (duplicate Model Number cannot be added; existing entry covers the changed variant). The published Model Number must exactly match whatever model/part number is printed on the actual shipped product's nameplate, label, manual, or catalog, since SIG market surveillance investigators search the Product List using that real-world string; every distinct color code or variant sold under its own number needs its own Product List derivative entry, while discontinued entries can simply remain as-is with no removal needed. The July 2024 Qualification Workspace migration rendered all previous procedure documents for derivative model additions obsolete; navigation to existing registrations changed to: My Blue icon → Qualification Workspace → Manage Submitted Products → checkbox filter.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Derivative model classification followed a strict two-condition test (same BLE FW + unchanged BLE-antenna path), with a third outcome when only the LC matching circuit changes (2-item RF PHY test required, but still a derivative not a new design). The SIG compliance principle that model number database searchability drives compliance enforcement was used to explain why duplicate Model Numbers in the Product List can't exist and why it's acceptable. Japan's Radio Act obligation was proactively surfaced when board or external appearance changes were mentioned, as a distinct regulatory obligation. When the SIG portal migration caused UI mismatch, the response was to immediately provide updated documentation for the new portal.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Treating a SoC-based design as a module-based design would omit required RF PHY testing, leaving the product without valid RF qualification. Failing to require the 2-item RF PHY test after an LC matching change could mean selling a product with unvalidated RF performance. Omitting the Radio Act 工事設計認証 re-application warning when board/enclosure changes are mentioned risks regulatory non-compliance under Japanese law. Using outdated procedure documents after the Qualification Workspace migration causes customers to fail derivative addition attempts and potentially delay product launches.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Proactively distinguish SoC-direct-mount vs. pre-certified-module paths at the quoting stage, as the cost and complexity difference is significant. Apply the two-condition derivative eligibility rule consistently (same BLE FW + unchanged BLE-antenna path = free derivative; LC matching change = 2-item test required derivative; other changes only = no test needed). Always surface Japan's Radio Act 工事設計認証 re-application requirements separately whenever board shape or external appearance changes are mentioned. When a customer reports a UI mismatch on the SIG website, immediately check whether the Qualification Workspace migration is the cause and provide updated procedure documents. Explain SIG compliance enforcement via database model-number search so customers understand why duplicate Model Numbers can't be added and why unchanged-model-number design changes don't require registration action.
